title: Janos Papai (Constantinople) to Ferenc Rakoczi II, 1706-1710, in the envoy key R580 (DECODE R740, R741, R757, R765, R784, R793-R796, R805, R823)

steps.what: Fetched the DECODE records, transcriptions and the R740 images with the project cookie.
Searched DECODE key records for NAH keys tagged Constantinople; R580 is headed 'key given to Janos Papai' (copies R581, R452).
Applied R581's table to R805: 336/336 groups give continuous Hungarian.
Applied the same table to R823, R765, R757, R741: 97.7-99.5% of groups in key.
Transcribed the numeric passage of R740 from the image (168 groups) and read it in full.
Web search for a printed decipherment: Benda 1963 edition of Papai's Turkish diaries exists, contents not checked.
Catalogue target 'Unknown sender to Rakoczi II, 1707' (DECODE R784): fetched record, transcription and both images.
Scored every NAH key record on DECODE (97 transcriptions) against R784; the Constantinople key R581 (Papai's) gave running Hungarian.
Read R784 with decode.py unchanged: 587/594 groups in key; French ambassador's report on the Porte and war.
Catalogue 47 'Constantinople envoys to Rakoczi II' (DECODE R793-R796): fetched four records and transcriptions; four despatches, not two.
Applied Papai's key R581 (decode.py) unchanged: R793/R794/R796 97.4-98.0% in key; R794 and R795 signed/dated Constantinople 1706.
R795 only 83.9% in key: 251 groups 323-740. Compared with the contemporary interlinear: the decipherer skips them, so nulls.
decode_nulls.py: 5,012 of 5,043 groups read (4,706 table values + 306 nulls), 31 slips.
Benda (ed.) 1963 edition of Papai's Turkish diaries: not online, antiquarian copies only.
decode2.py: split run-together groups, re-join split groups, 3-digit >322 as nulls (R823 clear numerals), 220 = a from context.
Second pass over the eleven numeric letters: 16,641 of 16,698 groups read (99.66%).
Rescored every remaining off-key group with the 4-gram model in context (retry_groups.py): no clear winner for the 57 left.

Entry split on 14 Oct 2026 under the one-key rule (George Lasry, 14 Oct 2026) from papai1706, which had joined Papai's eleven numeric letters in the envoy key R580/R581 with R731 (6 Mar 1710), whose passages are in a separate graphic-sign alphabet. This profile keeps the eleven numeric letters (R580 key) only.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): DECODE transcriptions DOC_<record>_*.txt (R740 transcribed here), second-pass readings <record>_read2.txt with the first-pass DOC_<record>_read.txt (R740: R740_read.txt); key R581/R580 transcriptions

Reading audit, per-document pass (George Lasry's sentence test): R795 re-read: its "·" marks are the 251 declared nulls (groups above 322), not gaps; without them the letter reads like the other ten. Per-document C overturned to B. Claim unchanged.

Verification 4: the nine Hungarian entries the sweep could not score (unspaced decodes) written out as word-divided readings (texts/<rec>_reading.md) from decode2 output, using the transcriber's copy of the contemporary interlinear decipherment where the DECODE file has it (R793, R794, R796), and the clear words inside R740's passage. Explicit-hole scores: R784 0.90, R741 0.718, R794 0.70, R765 0.698, R823 0.649, R757 0.628 (kept read, English written); R796 0.577, R793 0.529, R740 0.50 (demoted to decoded, not read).

r2g: R793 and R796 DECODE images (IMG_R793_I4441-4444, IMG_R796_I4453-4456) fetched with the project cookie (scratchpad only) and the digits checked line by line at native resolution against FK's transcriptions. R796: p. 1 l. 17 had been dropped and half of l. 18 repeated (the v4 'repeating letters'), nine further slips. R793: decode2.py had skipped eight figure lines that carry a <PLAINTEXT> tag; one p. 4 line missing in the transcription; about twenty split/joined/slipped groups; 98 (Constancz) in the date. Corrected copies texts/R79x_transcription_corrected.txt, changes in R79x_corrections.tsv; decoder research/reading_audit/r2g_papai_dec.py (decode2 rules, PLAINTEXT lines kept, --map for look-alike overrides).

r2g: R793 and R796 re-read word by word on the corrected decodes beside the interlinear decipherment copy; 87 (Moskva Ország) read as 81 'ar' in armistitium/articulus (4x in R796), 187 as 181 'bü' once (0.75% of letters). v2_score explicit holes: R796 0.577 -> 0.692, R793 0.529 -> 0.692. English written. Both decoded, not read -> read; R740 stays decoded, not read.
Consistency pass (cl): documents[].read for R805, R795, R740 read -> read in part, matching outcome.texts (decoded, not read) and fraction_read_source.
Read bar applied per document (v10): 7 of 8 documents marked read measure under 95% of words read as sense (v2_score explicit holes) and are now read in part; read_share recorded for each.

outcome.method_basis: DECODE key R580/R581, headed 'key given to János Pápai', from the same Rákóczi archive (MNL OL G15), was applied to DECODE's transcriptions of the eleven numeric letters and read 99.7% of groups.
outcome.fraction_read_source: decode2.py over the DECODE transcriptions of the eleven numeric letters: 16,641 of 16,698 numeric groups (nulls counted read); the ~41 tokens DECODE marks '?' added as unread: 16,641/~16,739. Before the split R731's ~330 signs were also counted unread (0.97). Verification 4, 23 Oct 2026: R796 (1,025), R793 (1,226) and R740 (168 groups) demoted to decoded, not read (0.857). r2g, 23 Oct 2026: R793 and R796 re-transcribed on the images and read; groups in letters that read, by the documents table: 16,693 of 16,861 = 0.990 (R740's 168 groups open).
outcome.notes: Eleven numeric letters read at 99.7% of groups after the second pass; 57 scattered groups (DECODE digit slips) and ~41 '?' tokens open, all blocked by the transcription. Split 14 Oct 2026: R731's graphic-sign passages are papai1710; on the eleven letters alone the read bar is met, so the class is read (was read in part).

texts.label: R805, 1 May 1706, Constantinople
texts.summary: The envoys urge that the Porte refuse the Imperial troops free passage across Ottoman ground, and that the border pashas, the Pasha of Arad among them, not allow the Germans passage towards Szeged without orders; they have spoken to the Vezír about their affairs and about Muscovy.

texts.note: 23 Oct 2026 (translation wave v7): does not read at decode level; most sentences have gaps, and some of the '·' marks taken as nulls hide letters (ke·elmes = kegyelmes). Needs the digits re-transcribed on the DECODE images as r2g did for R793/R796.
texts.label: R795, 1 Jan 1706, Constantinople
texts.summary: Pápai with Ferenc Horváth reports the Prince's discretion money handed to the Vezír's Kiaya, the Tatar Khan, the French ambassador, the Pasha of Temesvár, a Croatian incursion, and letters to go via Moldavia so that the Prince's news arrives faster.

texts.label: R796, 20 Feb 1706, Constantinople
texts.summary: The Prince's undated letter from the Tisza received; German false news believed neither by the Turks nor the confederates; the plea for those trapped in Moldavia blocked by the armistice articles, so the Moldavian kapukehaya and the serdar of Babadag (former pasha of Belgrade) are to be used; the Porte, frightened by the last war, will not prejudice the armistice nor help the Prince; nothing resolved on the propositions. Constantinople, 20 Feb 1706.

reading_review.note: r2g 23 Oct 2026: digits re-transcribed on the DECODE images IMG_R796_I4453-4456 (texts/R796_transcription_corrected.txt, R796_corrections.tsv: FK had dropped p. 1 l. 17 and repeated half of l. 18 - the 'repeating letters' of the v4 check - plus nine slips) and decoded with r2g_papai_dec.py (decode2 rules), read beside the transcriber's copy of the interlinear decipherment. v2_score explicit holes 0.692 (18/26), hole rate 0.106, 310 words (plain 0.077: the hu word list does not know 1706 spelling). Look-alike alternates: 87 read as 81 'ar' four times (armistitium, articulus), 187 as 181 'bü' once (with the interlinear decipherer): 10 of ~1,330 letters, 0.75%. Judged as a reader: the sentences hold except the closing lines before the signature. Grade B.

texts.note: 24 Oct 2026: 89.2% of the words of texts/R796_reading.md read as sense (v2_score explicit holes); coherent sentences but under the 95% read bar, so read in part.

texts.label: R793, 16 Mar 1706, Constantinople
texts.summary: Secret approaches to the Porte through the chancellor and the mufti about the unratified Muscovite peace and the Tana (Azov) frontier; with Sweden on the other side Poland could not hold out, and the Emperor is tied down by the French and Hungarian war; the Muscovite advances among the Astrakhanians, Circassians and Mingrelians and on the Black Sea; the Vizier asks whether the Hungarians would ally with Sweden; the Prince's manifesto translated and given to the Vizier; the envoy will pay nothing. Constantinople, 16 Mar 1706.

reading_review.note: r2g 23 Oct 2026: digits re-transcribed on the DECODE images IMG_R793_I4441-4444 (texts/R793_transcription_corrected.txt, R793_corrections.tsv): decode2.py had skipped every figure line that also carried a <PLAINTEXT> tag (eight lines), FK had left out one line of p. 4 and dropped 98 (Constancz) in the date, and about twenty groups were split, joined or slipped; decoded with r2g_papai_dec.py and read beside the transcriber's copy of the interlinear decipherment. v2_score explicit holes 0.692 (27/39), hole rate 0.085, 471 words (plain 0.0: 1706 spelling). Look-alike alternates: none. Judged as a reader: most sentences hold; the Black Sea passage (p. 2 ll. 14-24) and one name on p. 1 remain in outline. Grade B. Date: 'tizenhatodik Martius' = 16 March 1706.

texts.note: 24 Oct 2026: 91.4% of the words of texts/R793_reading.md read as sense (v2_score explicit holes); coherent sentences but under the 95% read bar, so read in part.

texts.label: R784, undated [1707], unsigned
texts.summary: The French ambassador reported that no arguments could bring the Porte to war, though the grandees and the whole Turkish nation incline to it; France means to turn Turkey wholly against the Germans, which would harm Hungary; if Muscovy and Poland do not second it, the Germans will overrun Hungary. A note in another hand asks the Prince to keep it secret and decipher it himself.
